title: Filter error lines from file content
prompt: Implement `std::string error_lines(const std::string& content)` that treats `content` as a text file (lines separated by \n) and returns only the lines starting with `ERROR `, each followed by \n. Use `std::istringstream` + `std::getline`.

tests.name: mixed
tests.code:
std::string out = error_lines(std::string{"INFO ok
ERROR bad
INFO fine
ERROR worse
"});
CHECK(out == std::string{"ERROR bad
ERROR worse
"});
tests.hint: Keep order; drop everything not starting with the prefix.

tests.name: prefix-only
tests.hint: The prefix must start at position 0.

tests.name: no-trailing-newline
tests.hint: The final line may lack \n — getline still yields it.
